newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Oct CPI rises 5.1 pct - government.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Oct CPI rises 5.1 pct - government.

text.p: South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 5.1 percent in October on the year, up from a 4.4 percent rise a year earlier, Ministry of Finance and Economy figures showed on Wednesday.
A ministry official said the year-on-year CPI rise in October was higher than a year earlier due largely to a sharp rise in import prices for crude oil.
"Crude import prices rose to $21 per barrel from $15 a year ago," said the official. "As a result, consumer prices for oil products rose a year-on-year 14.1 percent in October."
Food prices rose a year-on-year 4.0 percent in October, compared with a 2.1 percent rise a year earlier.
The ministry figures showed prices for agricultural, livestock and fisheries products increased a year-on-year 2.3 percent, while those for industrial products rose 3.1 percent.
Prices for public utilities, including bus fares, rose a year-on-year 10 percent in October, and charges for personal services increased 7.3 percent, the ministry figures showed.
The CPI, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, rose 4.7 percent for the whole of 1995, down from a 5.6 percent rise in 1994, the ministry said.
It said the CPI rise would be around 4.5 percent this year.
